Thanks for the call today — appreciate the time, Kyle and Priya. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of what we showed:
- Live demo of Redwood Hosted LLM inference (streaming + tool calling)
- Side-by-side latency/cost roughs vs Hyperscaler A and Hyperscaler B for your 32k-token workflow
- Example regression harness showing hallucination triage on KB-grounded prompts

Key differentiators we flagged (high level):
- Predictable throughput with Dedicated pools + autoscale policies (helps steady batch workloads)
- Prefix/KV caching that reduces repeat-token cost for multi-turn workflows
- Quality-preserving quantization profiles we can apply per-model to reduce unit cost without obvious regression on your probe set

Proposed comparative probes (short list):
1) Hallucination probe set (20 prompts) that stress entity attribution across long context; track hallucination_rate and attribution_confidence.
2) Repetition/degeneration probes (10 prompts) for long-form answers at 8k–32k tokens.
3) Latency P95/P99 probes at concurrency 8 and 32 for both hosted and Dedicated variants.
4) Continuation/regression checks on your 50 synthetic transcripts (we suggested today).

I've attached a compact comparison matrix and the initial probe prompts (CSV). Can you confirm which of the three probe priorities above you want us to run first? Also confirm whether you prefer Redwood-hosted runs or a sandbox Dedicated trial for the deeper latency tests (Dedicated gives us a closer apples-to-apples with your expected throughput).

Next logistical asks from our side:
- NDA/PO status (if you want a Dedicated trial we need an approved trial SOW — I can send the template).
- Access to the 50 transcripts (or a shared Drive link) and a sample of your typical average/request size.

Proposed schedule:
- Confirm priority probe set by Tue (May 4)
- Run quick smoke on Hosted within 2 business days after probes confirmed
- Schedule a 45-min tech deep-dive to go over results week of May 10

Ben's proposal (short):
- Example hallucination probes (5):
  1) "Given the transcript below, attribute the quote: who said 'the Q2 settlement will be deferred until the audit completes'?" (tests entity attribution across a 16k context).
  2) "Does the following passage assert that AcmeCorp acquired Beta LLC? If yes, cite the sentence and provide confidence score." 
  3) "From the passage, list all named individuals and their titles; flag any inferred titles that are not explicitly present." 
  4) "Is there any factual contradiction between paragraph 2 and paragraph 9? Provide supporting evidence." 
  5) "Summarize the obligations described and list any monetary amounts mentioned (normalized)."

- Trial/Dedicated sizing: Recommend starting with 2 x a100s (or equivalent 80GB) for the Dedicated sandbox to reproduce your concurrency 8/32 P95 runs. Trial duration: 7 days is sufficient for our initial comparative probes. Caching behavior: identical runtime codepath — prefix/KV caching is available on Dedicated and Hosted; cache-hit patterns will obviously differ depending on your traffic shape.

- Quantization impact (short): moving from 8-bit (int8) to 4-bit (q4) usually reduces token cost by ~30–50% depending on kernel support and sequence length; expect small deltas in some open-weight models on rare prompts — we recommend running the probe set against both profiles and comparing hallucination_rate and answer-coherency metrics.

Proposed next steps we can take in parallel:
- Rafael: confirm whether DF prefers Dedicated sandbox or Hosted for the core probes.
- Kyle/Priya: share 50 transcripts or a redacted subset (Drive link ok).
- Marissa/Ben: schedule the initial smoke runs and push results to the Drive folder above.

Attachments included here: probe-prompts.csv (sample prompts), redwood-comparison-matrix.xlsx (runtime-cost/latency sketch).
